newsitem.title: FRANCE: Juppe pledges to limit future rises in diesel duty.
newsitem.headline: Juppe pledges to limit future rises in diesel duty.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe pledged on Thursday that future rises in diesel duties would not exceed the rate of inflation.
"In 1997, the rise in duties will be reduced by more than a half compared to 1996, and brought to a level comparable to inflation," Juppe said in a letter to truck driver union leaders.
"The government will continue this policy, and the changes in duties over the following years will not exceed the rate of inflation," he said.
The pledge to limit future rises in diesel duties was designed to reassure truck drivers who blocked several key access roads into Paris on Thursday in protest against fuel taxes.

Limits in the rise in diesel duties were foreseen in the 1997 budget bill, unveiled in September, but Juppe took this a stage further on Thursday by promising to continue to cap the increase in future years.
In his letter he also promised that the government would ensure it defended truck drivers interests in any talks with its partners in the European Union on petrol duties.
